newsitem.title: CHINA: Bridge over Yellow River could hit Hong Kong cargo.
newsitem.headline: Bridge over Yellow River could hit Hong Kong cargo.

text.p: A planned bridge linking Hong Kong with the western Pearl River delta could have major long term implications for Hong Kong's freight industry, experts told Reuters.

The 53-km bridge would give Hong Kong freight forwarders access to lower cost, alternative airports such as Zhuhai and Macau. But it is unlikely to pose an immediate threat to Hong Kong's Chek Lap Kok airport due to open next year as the region's leading cargo destination.

In a recent interview in Hong Kong's South China Morning Post, the Communist Party secretary of the Zhuhai Special Economic Zone, Liang Guangda, said Beijing's go-ahead for building the Lingding toll bridge is awaited.

Once approved, foreign capital and construction groups will be welcome and Liang said actual contruction would take six years. It is one of a series of major transport projects in Guangdong province including an eight lane coastal expressway and a six lane road link to Beijing.
"When the bridge is complete, it will completely change the transport situation in southwest China. In Guangdong alone, the bridge will benefit nearly 30 million people," Liang said.
Major freight forwarders said links between Hong Kong and Macau and other airports in the Pearl River delta are inadequate but a bridge would change this.
"Because of high fees at Chek Lap Kok, more and more carriers might think about whether they should go to Macau and the bridge will make that decision easier," one said.
Aviation consultant Jim Eckes said cargo originating in the Pearl river Delta region, which traditionally has been trucked to Kai Tak airport in Hong Kong, could be sent to lower cost Zhuhai airport.
Zhuhai has the finest airport in China with excellent runway and terminal facilities but it's empty because the Chinese government only allows domestic flights, he said.
"If the bridge is in and tolls are reasonable I think some cargo will be sucked out of Hong Kong and into either Macau or Zhuhai because Chek Lap Kok will be a very expensive airport for cargo."

"The big advantage (Chep Lap Kok) has is that Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited (HACTL) is the most efficient operator anywhere in the world and some shippers are prepared to pay more for that service," Eckes added. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
